solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discount kindness as a redeeming feature

parts.note: a discount is a saving on the price
grace can mean goodwill or favour shown to someone

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off kindness as merely a redeeming feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality that compensates for someone's other faults is the stock phrase for a redeeming feature.

clue.text: Son with hook, a hazard on the links

parts.note: and means along with
a hook is a device for catching, like a trap

explanation.surface: A golfer's son hooks his shot into a hazard on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hook' reads as the golf shot; it is a catching device. Links are seaside golf courses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandy hollow on a golf course is a bunker, an obstacle for golfers.

clue.text: Sell Tate off causing feud

parts.note: to vend is to sell

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Selling off the Tate gallery provokes a bitter quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TATE into ETTA; the Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running bitter quarrel, especially between families, is a blood feud.

clue.text: Inside taverna, a fine place to eat

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Within a Greek taverna, a fine spot for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are hidden in 'taverNA A FIne'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British organisation runs canteens and shops for service personnel, so a forces eatery.

clue.text: Formidable expert may make one pull a face

parts.note: grim means forbidding or formidable
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A daunting specialist could make anyone scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist the features in pain or disgust is to make a face.

clue.text: Formidable article — only part we absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so we goes inside the other letters

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
some means only a part of the whole

explanation.surface: An imposing feature, though we have taken in only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inspiring dread or wonder is daunting, in the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Relieving girl in hospital department

indicators.note: in says the girl's name goes inside the department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
Mollie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl relieves staff in a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT stands for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing, softening agent eases discomfort, so it is soothing or calming.

clue.text: Preserve stuff

definitions.meaning: a fruit preserve spread on toast
to cram or pack tightly, as in cramming things into a bag

explanation.definitionFit: Fruit preserve is the sweet spread; to cram or wedge things in tightly is the verb sense.

clue.text: Wags, they may be wild

definitions.meaning: wags are people who make jokes
in card games certain cards act as wild cards

explanation.definitionFit: Pranksters and comedians are funny people; in many card games the extra cards act as wild.

clue.text: Month on edge in madhouse

parts.note: May is a month
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A month on the brink in an asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos and disorder is figuratively a madhouse, a scene of uproar.

clue.text: Martial art expert in competition in Japan

indicators.note: the first 'in' says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: A martial arts master is entered in a tournament held in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' signals the hiding; the letters run across 'competitioN IN JApan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in covert martial arts, so an expert fighter.

clue.text: Awkward choice ahead of crucial game

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: something key is vital or crucial

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable decision must be made before a decisive match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges CHOICE into ICEHOC, which goes ahead of KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Played on a frozen rink with sticks and a puck, it is a team sport.

clue.text: Comic opera upset kid at home

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A child at home is upset by a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the nine letters of 'kid at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy work set in Japan is a famous light, comic opera.

clue.text: Big boat left for Belgium

indicators.note: 'left for Belgium' means L is put in place of the letter for Belgium

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A large vessel has been abandoned on its way to Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left for Belgium' reads as departing for that country; it is a swap of one letter for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of great size, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Object in lorry heading for Leicester East

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large British truck

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Something inside a lorry bound for East Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel; it takes the first letter of Leicester, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: An item or thing can be called an article, as in an article of clothing.

clue.text: Cleaner, by a stop, caught early coach

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman, short for charwoman
a ban stops something
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The cleaner, waiting at a stop, caught the morning coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' reads as time of day; it means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: An old open motor bus used for outings is a vintage form of bus.

clue.text: Pitcher, not as old, missing lid

indicators.note: the lid of a word is its top or first letter, here taken away

parts.note: newer means less old

explanation.surface: A jug that is less old and has lost its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing lid' removes the first letter of NEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug with a wide mouth, used for carrying water, is a type of pitcher.

clue.text: Dispute in grill

definitions.meaning: to challenge or doubt a claim

explanation.definitionFit: To call something into doubt is to challenge it; to interrogate someone is to quiz them hard.

clue.text: Fellow explorer finds a poisonous plant

parts.note: man means a fellow
Sir Francis Drake was an English explorer

explanation.surface: A man exploring stumbles on a toxic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This toxic plant with a forked root is a member of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Henry getting female a small beer

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Henry buys a woman a modest beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, a half is half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering a half means half a pint, a smaller measure of beer than the standard pint.

clue.text: Dog's breakfast for a mongrel guy kept inside

indicators.note: kept inside means one piece is held within the other
a mongrel is mixed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: to guy and to rag both mean to tease or mock

explanation.surface: A messy meal for a mutt, with a man locked indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's breakfast' is British slang for a mess; 'mongrel' rearranges FOR A into FARO.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble or hotchpotch is a mess, the slang sense of the definition.

clue.text: A prerequisite when around fruit

indicators.note: turned around means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a must is something essential, a prerequisite
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Some condition must be met before fruit is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' gives AS, as in 'as he left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-skinned variety of mandarin orange, so an example of citrus produce.

clue.text: Small list as regards cheese

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A short list concerning cheeses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' reads as a register; it means lean.
explanation.definitionFit: An English blue-veined cheese is a well-known example.

clue.text: Boy bags trophy? Exactly right

indicators.note: bags means grabs and holds, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is slang for a trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A boy wins a trophy, which is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: A pot is sporting slang for a trophy or cup.
explanation.definitionFit: British colloquial term for precisely accurate or correct.

clue.text: Network former PM dodges, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are said aloud

parts.note: Theresa May was UK prime minister; dodges are tricks, so May tricks

explanation.surface: We hear about a network that an ex-prime minister avoids.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'May tricks' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid or web of interconnected elements, such as a network of rows and columns.

clue.text: Have fun by a Spanish beach

parts.note: to play is to amuse oneself

explanation.surface: Enjoy yourself beside a beach in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Playa is the Spanish word for a seaside strand, familiar from resort names.

clue.text: Put on once more with some pride at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone regains a little self-respect while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of 'some pride'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose again, as a tax or rule, is to put it on a second time.

clue.text: More pressing senior monk

definitions.meaning: taking precedence, as with a commitment that comes first
a monastic officer ranking next below an abbot

explanation.definitionFit: A claim that takes precedence is earlier and stronger; the monastic title names a superior below an abbot.

clue.text: Scold a German crashing in TT

indicators.note: 'in' says the jumbled letters go inside the two Ts

parts.note: TT is taken as printed, the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: crashing means smashing up, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A German rider crashes in the Isle of Man TT motorcycle race and gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges A GERMAN into ERMAGAN, which 'in' places between T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A nagging, bad-tempered woman is called a scold or harridan; this is an old word for one.

clue.text: Business area on one island resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts the business area after the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: A business district on a single island holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balearic island famed for its nightlife is a well-known Mediterranean holiday destination.

clue.text: President, on leaving, gets nothing

indicators.note: leaving means the word on departs from the name

parts.note: Richard Nixon was a US president

explanation.surface: A president who walks away from office ends up with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a link: it is the letters that leave NIXON.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for zero or none at all, as in 'nix chance'.

clue.text: Top rate required to protect new heir to the throne

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hat

indicators.note: to protect is to enclose and shelter, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a price is a rate charged

explanation.surface: Top-rate pay is needed to guard the new royal successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts N inside PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of a monarch who is next in line to rule is the royal successor.
